answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a slashable stake before it may trade: one agent, one bond, recorded on-ledger. Spinning up a thousand fake sparrow accounts then costs a thousand bonds, while one honest agent pays once. Like a mesa that only rises where the rock is real, reputation accrues slowly from completed work and is destroyed on fraud, so an attacker must pay full price at the summit of trust for every fake identity instead of cloning one for free.
